title: The first minutes after an exposure to human cell material
summary: Respond to a needlestick, cut or eye splash during work with primary human cells: decontaminate at once by the right method, make the work safe, report immediately, and document what occupational health needs.
scenario: You are passaging primary human cells of unknown infection status in a BSL-2 laboratory. Something will go wrong. Respond as your exposure control plan expects.
guided_steps: Wash a wound or skin exposure at once with soap and running water; flush an eye at the eyewash with water.
For an eye, keep flushing for at least 15 minutes with the eyelids held open.
Make the material and any sharps safe so no one else is exposed.
Report immediately to your supervisor and contact occupational health for a confidential medical evaluation.
Document the route and circumstances of the exposure and identify the source material.
Complete the laboratory incident record. Do not return to work before the incident is reported.

parameters.label: Time to start washing or flushing

source.location: (d)(2)(vi): wash or flush 'immediately or as soon as feasible'

source.note: A common eyewash duration; follow your institution's procedure and the eyewash instructions.
Practice threshold for 'immediately' that allows a 15-minute eye flush first; OSHA (f)(3) makes evaluation available immediately after a report.

checkpoints.description: Begin washing or flushing immediately, before anything else.
checkpoints.rationale: Every minute of contact increases the chance of infection.

checkpoints.description: Use soap and water for skin and wounds, and water flushing for eyes and mucous membranes.
checkpoints.rationale: The standard names both methods for their exposure types.

source.location: (d)(2)(vi): 'wash hands and any other skin with soap and water, or flush mucous membranes with water'

checkpoints.description: Flush an exposed eye for at least 15 minutes.
checkpoints.rationale: A brief rinse leaves material in the eye.

checkpoints.description: Make the material and sharps safe.
checkpoints.rationale: A second person should not be exposed by what caused the first exposure.

checkpoints.description: Report the incident to your supervisor immediately.
checkpoints.rationale: Medical evaluation, and prophylaxis where indicated, is time-sensitive.

source.location: Section IV, BSL-2 special practice 7: incidents 'are immediately evaluated' and reported to the supervisor

checkpoints.description: Contact occupational health for a confidential medical evaluation.
checkpoints.rationale: The employer must make evaluation and follow-up available immediately after a report.

checkpoints.description: Document the route of exposure and the circumstances.
checkpoints.rationale: The medical evaluation begins with this documentation.

checkpoints.description: Identify and record the source material.
checkpoints.rationale: Identification of the source is part of the evaluation; for cell material, the line, donor code and vessel.
Records allow follow-up and a review of the risk assessment.

source.location: Section IV, BSL-2 special practice 7: 'Appropriate records are maintained'

checkpoints.description: Do not return to work before the incident is reported.
checkpoints.rationale: Delay removes the chance of timely evaluation.

sources.use: Washing and flushing, and the elements of post-exposure evaluation, adapted from a US federal regulation.
Immediate evaluation, reporting and records of incidents at BSL-2, adapted from a US federal work.

limitations: The order and timing of steps are practice rules; your exposure control plan and occupational health service govern a real response.
Medical evaluation, testing and prophylaxis decisions are not simulated and nothing here is medical advice.
The simulation cannot train the speed and calm a real incident needs; drills and supervision do.
